children: Trade Desk announced Friday it's significantly reducing its workforce. Wall Street approved the move.

Shares of Trade Desk advanced 3.3% to $15.58 in premarket trading on Friday after the advertising technology company said it plans to decrease its workforce by 15% as part of a broad restructuring effort.

The company in a regulatory filing said it plans to implement an organizational realignment to focus on long-term growth. Trade Desk, as part of the plan, will reduce its total workforce by about 15%. The company expects the headcount reductions to be mostly completed during the third quarter.
Trade Desk estimated restructuring charges of around $39 million to $51 million related to employee severance and benefits costs in the third quarter.

Trade Desk stock has dropped 60% this year and has underperformed the broader market. The company in early August missed second-quarter revenue expectations and management at the time said the company was "taking decisive action to strengthen our execution, upgrade our platform, and sharpen our focus."
